features.title: Local OTLP/HTTP receiver
features.summary: The Host listens on a loopback OTLP/HTTP port (4318 by default) and accepts POST /v1/traces in JSON and protobuf, gzip or deflate, from any OpenTelemetry exporter; spans are validated, bounded and stored with whole-trace retention. Plugin, external and both modes decide whether this receiver owns the port and whether it forwards to an external viewer.

configuration.constraints: plugin: this receiver owns the port; external: receiver off; both: store and forward to forwardUrl.
0 to 65535; 0 picks any free port. A port held by another process is reported and retried every 30 s.
A non-loopback host is refused unless this is on.
GenAI message, prompt and tool-payload attributes are stored as their size only.
1,000 to 1,000,000 spans; whole traces drop oldest first, alongside retentionHours (default 72).

failureModes: A body over 8 MiB, or one that inflates past 32 MiB, is rejected with 413/400 instead of being buffered.
A malformed protobuf or JSON body is rejected with 400 and nothing is stored.
A port held by another process (another collector, dsh-traces) leaves stored traces browsable and says so in the panel.
A non-loopback listen address is refused unless explicitly allowed.
A forward URL that points back at the receiver is ignored, so telemetry never loops.
GenAI content attributes are stored as their size unless redaction is turned off.

externalDependencies.boundary: OTLP/HTTP POST bodies (opentelemetry-proto v1 ExportTraceServiceRequest) from any exporter: LoongSuite (protobuf), dshx tracing (JSON), or a third-party SDK.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Request bodies are produced by the official @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer serializers in unit tests and by a synthetic OTLP JSON payload in the browser journey.

verification.testName: stores protobuf, gzip protobuf and JSON trace bodies and answers in kind
rejects wrong paths, methods, media types, oversize and malformed bodies
reports a port held by another process and keeps the rest of the status

rejects a truncated protobuf body
replaces content attributes with their size, also on events
keeps content attributes as sent when redaction is turned off
bounds names, attribute counts, string values and events
drops whole traces past the age and span limits, and clears everything

features.title: Trace list and span waterfall
features.summary: A Traces panel lists stored traces newest first with filters (text, service, error status, minimum duration) kept across reloads; opening one shows a collapsible span waterfall on a time axis, colored by service with errors in red, and a side panel with the selected span's attributes, events and resource attributes, plus an Open thread link when a span carries dsh.session.id.
failureModes: A span whose parent never arrived is shown as a root rather than dropped.
A trace pruned while open reports that it is no longer stored.
A dsh.session.id for a thread this Host does not list is reported unavailable instead of opening anything.
A forged pagination cursor is rejected by the Host.

verification.testName: lists traces newest first with root, duration, counts, services and session
filters by service, operation, status, duration, time, text and session
pages with a cursor and rejects a forged one
returns one trace as a depth-first tree with offsets and resource attributes
treats a span whose parent is missing as a root
hides the descendants of collapsed spans only

features.title: Log search with trace correlation
features.summary: The receiver also accepts POST /v1/logs (JSON or protobuf); the Logs tab searches stored records newest first by text, service, minimum severity and one attribute value, a record with a trace id opens its trace, and a span or trace opens only its own logs. GenAI content events keep only their body size unless redaction is turned off.

configuration.constraints: 1,000 to 1,000,000 records; the oldest go first, alongside retentionHours.

failureModes: A record without a time or observed time is rejected and counted.
A log whose trace was pruned still lists; opening it reports that the trace is no longer stored.
A forged logs cursor is rejected by the Host.

verification.testName: decodes SDK log records from protobuf into the same records as from JSON
keeps severity, body, attributes, event name and the trace correlation
stores protobuf and JSON log bodies on /v1/logs
searches logs by service, severity, text, attribute, trace and span, newest first with paging
drops the oldest logs past the count limit and expired ones by age

features.title: Service and operation overview, error groups
features.summary: A service strip and an Operations tab summarize span volume, error rate and p50/p95/p99 latency per service and operation over a chosen window; an Errors tab groups error spans by service, operation, error type and message shape with counts, first and last seen and a sample trace.
failureModes: Percentiles use the nearest-rank method, so a single sample is its own p50, p95 and p99.
Error messages that differ only by numbers fold into one group.

verification.testName: summarizes services and operations over a window
groups errors by service, operation, type and message shape
uses nearest-rank percentiles
every traces capability is a named tool and only clear writes
